# Ein Sof Captions — Runtime Proof and Completion Review

The Awtsmoos brought the hidden worker through every layer into a visible completed light;
Awtsmoos.com now has measured evidence that the simple studio shell and advanced renderer meet in one working sight.

## Original plan

- Replace the 893-line monolith with a preview-first responsive studio.
- Keep only essentials visibly open; advanced controls live in retractable native disclosures.
- Preserve every renderer control, default, randomization behavior, IndexedDB contract, directory-picker option, fallback download, 1080×1920 render size, and filename convention.
- Replace inline blob Worker code with a readable module-worker graph.
- Keep every source <=120 lines without compressed code.
- Make desktop rail retractable and mobile controls off-canvas.
- Remove continuous pulse/flicker chrome and honor reduced motion.
- Test architecture first, then geometry/state/persistence, then a real renderer result.

## What was actually written

The static page is now a small readable shell. Five control panels are generated from declarative definitions before DOM services initialize. Main-thread concerns are split across DOM collection, panel/input rendering, randomization, storage codec/transport, settings collection, drawer state, downloads, preview, and worker coordination. Worker concerns are split across palette/randomness, background/stars, particle universe/rendering, spatially indexed networks, typography layout/painting/vessel, bloom, post-processing, final B\"H/ב\"ה marks, orchestration, and entry messaging.

## Verification evidence

Architecture gate:
- Largest source file: 115 lines.
- All JavaScript passes `node --check`.
- No source line exceeds 160 characters after anti-cramping refactor.
- Every local import and HTML CSS/JS reference resolves.
- No four-digit z-index, legacy 500px/540px/960px fixed geometry, or infinite UI animation remains.

Measured UI acceptance:
- Desktop 1440×900: 0 horizontal/vertical document overflow, 430×764 preview frame, 390px studio, only Essentials open initially.
- Desktop retraction: studio contracts 390px → 58px and `aria-expanded` becomes false.
- Mobile 390×844: 0 document overflow, 374×665 preview, off-canvas studio.
- Short phone 320×568: 0 document overflow, 304×492 preview.
- Numeric randomization reveals range and disables fixed value while active.
- Color randomization stays range-free while active.
- Mobile live diagnostic proved Controls adds `is-open`, moves panel to x=0, reveals backdrop, and sets `aria-expanded=true`.
- IndexedDB write/read proved `userSettings.boxPadding=77`; bounded hydration restored 77 after reload.
- Added explicit `data-ein-sof-ready=true` plus `einsofready` event so future tests never confuse DOM load with hydrated app readiness.

Real worker render acceptance against healthy static server:
- Ready contract resolved.
- Low-density smoke settings intentionally disabled connections/grain/bloom only to reduce test cost.
- Canvas pixels changed from the initial preview sample.
- Worker/status completed with `Complete · 1 vision`.
- Exactly one JPEG download was requested.
- Filename preserved `BH_<timestamp>_EinSof_<sanitized>_1.jpg` semantics.
- Generate was re-enabled after completion.
- Canvas remained exactly 1080×1920.
- Document horizontal overflow remained 0.
- Zero runtime exceptions were captured.

## Important false-positive archaeology

Two acceptance failures were infrastructure/harness defects, not app defects:
1. An old Python server remained listening after tunnel restart but returned `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` to Chrome. Replacing it with a fresh HTTP-200 server removed the false readiness failure.
2. Immediate post-reload storage checks read before async IndexedDB hydration. A bounded live diagnostic proved the persisted value restores correctly; the new explicit readiness contract eliminates this ambiguity going forward.

## Improvements beyond the original plan

- Catalog exposure and main discovery were completed before this renderer rewrite, so the engine is not merely fixed but publicly discoverable.
- Network neighbor search now uses 400px spatial cells rather than repeatedly sorting the whole particle population for every particle, preserving visible semantics while removing an obvious high-density performance trap.
- Persistence now serializes an explicit manifest instead of every arbitrary element with an id.
- Worker errors and main-thread save failures both recover the Generate button rather than trapping the user in a disabled state.
- Declarative control definitions replace a second-generation HTML compression trap discovered during self-review.

## Remaining work created by this success

The Ein Sof engine itself has crossed its architecture + UI + persistence + renderer acceptance gate. The broader project is not complete. Next gravity nodes are newly exposed Adventure and Ohrbound gameplay/mobile surfaces, DB Console form/mobile behavior, Broadcaster responsive foundations, final isolated Video Editor interaction acceptance, and continued global app/game overlay/focus/HUD sweep.
